messages.subject: Re: Instance with different files
messages.body_plain:
Thank you Manuel for such valuable information.

Le mardi 28 août 2018 05:53:17 UTC-4, Manuel López-Ibáñez a écrit :
> Hi Ines,
>
> You can create an instances.txt file, where each line describes a different instance. Then your target-runner will interpret what the file says is an instance and read the appropriate files. Something like:
>
> instance-A-1
> instance-A-2
> instance-A-3
> instance-B-1
> instance-B-2
>
> Then, set
> trainInstancesDir=""
> trainInstancesFile="instances.txt"
>
> This way, irace will not look for files in trainInstancesDir, it will just pass individual lines from instances.txt (which do not need to correspond to any file, they are just a string of text) to target-runner. Then, your target-runner will receive something like "instance-X-Y" from irace and understand that it means reading files "X" and "Y".  The lines in "instances.txt" can be even more complicated. It depends how you parse this information in your target-runner.
>
> I recommend using "--check" first, to see what information is irace sending to your target-runner.
>
> I hope the above helps!
>
> Manuel.
>
> On Sunday, 26 August 2018 15:02:40 UTC+1, ines methlouthi wrote:
> > Hi Irace community,
> > I am a new member, and I try to use irace to tune my parameters. The problem is that each one of my instances is composed of différent files. I saved each instance in one directory and all the directories are under /Instances. When I launch Irace, he considers each file a different instance.
> > did someone know a trick to consider each directory one instance. ??
> >
> > Thank you in advance.
> >

Hi Ines,

Are you sure the last line of your program is just that number? The error says that target-runner returned:

-123334.984375

That is, if you run:

/Users/mkrimi/target-runner 1 1 801596601 /Users/mkrimi/Instances/CdB-N-40-40-50-3tech-inst1    85 113 65 0.58248 0.01649

You'll see that output, which irace does not recognize as valid (it is not a number).

Maybe try to see what the stdout file contains for the above call.

Cheers,

Manuel.
